headline: Maui County Council Meeting - (recessed from 9/25/26 mtg)

meeting.body: Maui County Council Meeting - (recessed from 9/25/26 mtg)
meeting.summary: The Council voted 5–4 to adopt a committee report backing a resolution asking the Maui Planning Commission to consider hotel zoning for coastal apartment properties.
meeting.recap: The only item was Committee Report 26-68, which recommends adopting Resolution 26-129 CD1.[[0:30:00]] The resolution asks the Maui Planning Commission to consider hotel zoning for certain apartment properties in coastal hazard areas.[[0:30:05]] The change would let transient vacation rentals (short-term rentals to visitors) continue at those properties.[[0:30:28]] The committee included properties with more than half of their building footprints in sea level rise, flood hazard or shoreline setback areas.[[0:34:44]] The committee said these properties can be hard and expensive to maintain and may not suit long-term housing.[[0:34:56]] A council member moved to add two more properties in Lahaina to the list.[[0:39:00]] On that amendment, the clerk reported four ayes and five noes.[[0:43:59]] A council member said the Planning Commission approved five of 48 properties from an earlier resolution.[[0:49:30]] A council member voting no said the 32-property list was unfair to volunteer commissioners.[[0:57:22]] Tamara Paltin said it is dangerous to let these shoreline properties stay short-term rentals.[[1:03:22]] Vice Chair Sugimura supported moving the resolution to the Planning Commission for review.[[1:16:14]] The Council adopted the committee report with five ayes and four noes.[[1:23:26]]
meeting.next: The Planning Commission is to review the bills, hold public hearings and issue findings before final Council action.
